title-proc.eng: Multi beam echo sounder update

description-proc.eng: Kartverket ́s measuring boats are originally built with Kongsberg EM2040 systems 'flush mounted' in the hull. Both the hull design, integration and production track are adapted to this system. Kartverket has good experience with the current installation and work methodology. The systems provide the data quality and coverage required for the Norwegian Mapping Authority ́s operative assignment. The system is simultaneously adapted to the metering boats ́ usage patterns, including the need for high logging and transit speed and high operational security under demanding conditions. It has been assessed whether alternative tenderers and assembly systems can be relevant when holding a tender contest. Kartverket has examined the available alternative suppliers and assembly systems in the assessment. The review has included a review of available products in the market, where, among other things, the technical product specifications have been assessed. Based on this survey, an alternative system has not been identified that can be installed in the existing vessel without extensive technical adaptations. Technical assessments suggest that this will involve extensive changes in the hull and installation, as well as the need for new surveying and new CFD analysis. This is expected to lead to considerable costs, technical and operational risk and downtime. In addition there is a risk that the vessels ́ existing speed characteristics and operative qualities will be affected. If different echo sounder systems are established on the measuring boats, the Norwegian Mapping Authority must administer and operationalise two different systems. This will increase the technical and operative complexity and be able to lead to increased costs and resource need over time. For Kartverket it is important to maintain a joint echo sounder system on the measuring boats in order to ensure interoperability between the vessels. This gives, among other things, the possibility to move equipment between the vessels as needed, as well as to use the same competence, work methodology and system management across the measuring boats. The standardisation of the echo sounder system is therefore assessed as a clear operational advantage and it contributes to greater flexibility, simple management and reduced operational risk. Alternative mounting modes, including pole assembly, are also considered. Such systems are not considered suitable for taking care of The Norwegian Mapping Authority's total operative needs in the same way as a hull mounted system. The measuring boats operate year-round in demanding conditions and require high operational security, high logging and transit speed and robust systems at low risk for mechanical challenges and interruptions to operations. An alternative assembly system will therefore involve a different operative system than the current Norwegian Mapping Authority. Kartverket therefore believes that there are technical reasons why the echo sounder can be procured directly from Kongsberg Discovery pursuant to the Public Procurement Regulations §§ 13-4 b) (2). The assessment is based on the fact that, due to technical reasons, there is not a real alternative that can cover The Norwegian Mapping Authority's need without extensive adaptations of the vessels, and that there is not a reasonable alternative or replacement system that can be procured through competition without this resulting in significant technical and operative consequences. In this case, other echo sounders are not compatible with the existing mounting system in the measuring boats. This must be seen in connection with KOFA practice, where the technical and economic consequences of alternative solutions are included in the assessment of whether there is a real and reasonable alternative, cf. Alternative suppliers must offer systems that involve comprehensive technical adaptations, including alterations to the hull, installation and new surveying of the vessels, and will not be able to continue the vessels ́ existing operative qualities without significant adaptations. According to Kartverket ́s assessment, a competition will not be suitable for providing a real competitive alternative. In total Kongsberg Discovery EM2042 is considered as the only system that can continue the existing hull mounted system without extensive alterations and new surveying of the vessels. Kartverket primarily assesses that the terms in the Public Procurement Regulations § 13-4 letter b no. 2 have been met. After a technical assessment, no other supplier or solution has been identified that can cover The Norwegian Mapping Authority's needs without extensive technical adaptations of the vessels. A supplier change will involve significant technical and operative consequences, including alterations to the hull and installation, new surveying, increased downtime and risk of influencing the vessels ́ existing operative qualities. Kartverket considers, on this basis, that there is not a real and reasonable alternative that can be procured through a competition and that the condition that competition is impossible for technical reasons has been met. Kartverket therefore assesses that the procurement can be made without a competition pursuant to PPR § 13-4 letter b no. 2, and subsidiary letter c.

title-proc.eng: 10035189-Advice on implementation of AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol and technical inputs to related reforms; facilitation and development of partnerships with the private sector on digital trade

description-proc.eng: The project "Pan-African e-Commerce Initiative 3 - Boosting African Digital Trade" (PeCI 3) is a regional technical cooperation project implemented by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) in the context of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The project aims to strengthen an enabling environment for cross-border digital trade in Africa, with a particular focus on micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), including women-led businesses. PeCI 3 contributes to the BMZ"s core area "Sustainable Economic Development, Training and Employment" and supports it"s digital policy and Africa Strategy through the promotion of inclusive digital trade ecosystems, and public-private cooperation. The project builds on the achievements and partnerships established under the previous phases (PeCI 1 and PeCI 2). Earlier phases supported MSMEs in adopting e-commerce solutions and digital sales channels, strengthened intermediary organisations providing training and advisory services, facilitated public-private exchange on digital trade issues and contributed to regional approaches related to e-commerce, digital payments, consumer protection and electronic transactions. The project also strengthened cooperation with the East African Community (EAC), the Smart Africa Alliance (SAA) and the AfCFTA Secretariat. PeCI 3 supports implementation of the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol (DTP), adopted by the African Union in 2024, by strengthening structures, processes and cooperation mechanisms required for cross-border digital trade. The project addresses barriers affecting MSME participation in digital trade, including fragmented regulatory frameworks, limited interoperability of digital payment systems, logistics and last-mile delivery challenges, gaps in online consumer protection and limited coordination between public and private actors. Particular attention is given to barriers affecting women"s participation in digital trade ecosystems. The project operates at pan-African, regional and national levels and combines technical advisory services, stakeholder consultations, public-private dialogue formats and capacity development measures. Activities include support for implementation of selected DTP chapters, facilitation of cross-border exchange on best practices, development of cooperation models between private-sector actors and intermediary organisations, and support for gender-sensitive approaches to digital entrepreneurship and MSME support services. Environmental sustainability is integrated as a cross-cutting topic, including approaches related to sustainable packaging and resource-efficient logistics. The project is implemented in cooperation with public, private and regional stakeholders in selected AfCFTA countries, particularly Ghana and Kenya, as well as with the EAC. Lead executing agencies are the Ministry of Finance in Ghana, the Ministry of Investments, Trade and Industry (MITI) in Kenya and the EAC Secretariat. Additional partners include the AfCFTA Secretariat, the Smart Africa Secretariat, chambers of commerce, business and e-commerce associations, payment service providers, logistics companies, innovation hubs and women"s business networks. PeCI 3 further aims to strengthen cooperation between African, German and European private-sector actors to promote cross-border digital trade and MSME participation. The project cooperates with business associations, e-commerce platforms, logistics and payment providers, chambers of commerce and innovation actors, including bevh, AHKs and African e-commerce associations. Cooperation with UNCTAD, ITC and initiatives supported by the European Union and the World Bank further strengthens synergies and regional outreach. The project is scheduled to run until June 2028.

title-proc.eng: Supply Delivery and Installation of Dual-Inlet Isotope-Ratio Mass Spectrometer

description-proc.eng: The instrument will be used for high-precision (order 0.001‰) measurements of dissolved N2 in water samples, via dual-inlet analyses. Dissolved gas samples will be extracted, purified, and transferred offline into the detachable dip tubes, that can be connected to one side of the dual inlet. The other side will be attached to a custom reference gas comprising N2, Ar, and Kr. A suitably qualified Quantity Surveyor (QS) is also required as part of the team to prepare robust costs estimates, including life cycle costs (as required by Circular 17/25), in accordance with the International Cost Management Standards 3 (ICMS3), as mandated by the Capital Works Management Framework (CWMF). DAFM has already completed extensive preparatory work including computational modelling, site investigations, engineering designs, and cost estimations for a long-list and shortlist of options to address the problematic wave dynamics in the harbour. The successful Consultant shall be required to review all existing data in advance of commencing their work. The objective of this commission is to ensure the following:  Full compliance with the Infrastructure Guidelines by undertaking the Strategic Assessment before the development of a full Preliminary Business Case  Upon approval of the Strategic Assessment, prepare the Preliminary Business Case for full and formal Approval-in-Principle i.e. progression through Approval Gate 1  Upon approval, preparation of the Stage 1 reports per Guidance Note 1.2 of the Capital Works Management Framework (CWMF) culminating in the preparation of the Definitive Project Brief that will form the basis for Stage ii Detailed Design (not part of this commission)  Engage with key stakeholders during all stages of the commission and ensure their views are fully considered in the development of the reports

title-proc.eng: Contract for the Provision for the Manufacture of Vaccine Antigen

description-proc.eng: UCD has developed a series of bacterial antigens which have proven effective in proof-of-concept studies and which the aim is to further develop and translate to humans. The lead target antigen is 22 kDa cytosolic bacterial protein and is currently His-tagged to facilitate affinity purification. UCD have developed a lab-scale expression and purification protocol, which will be provided to the successful contractor. We require contract protein manufacture and purification services. The purpose of the work is to appropriately scale-up the antigen to produce ~200mg batches of protein at a standard that will confirm feasibility of technology transfer and that can be used in GLP toxicology studies in mice, to ensure safety of the developed product. Ultimately, UCD would like the process to be amenable to production in a GMP facility in the future.

title-proc.eng: Second phase of the EU assistance for Uzbekistan Agri-Food Development Strategy 2020-2030

description-proc.eng: This is the Second phase of the EU assistance for Uzbekistan Agri-Food Development Strategy 2020-2030, under the ongoing Financing Agreement with the Government of Uzbekistan ACT- 61294 "Budget Support for the development of Agri-food sector and resilient rural livelihoods". The purpose of this contract is to pursue the assistance to the Government of Uzbekistan in managing the transition process from a planned economy to a market-based system by creating an enabling policy and regulatory environment and strengthening key institutional capacities, with a particular focus on food safety, water management, rangeland and agricultural land planning, agricultural subsidies, agricultural extension services, agricultural subsidies, and public finance management. The main recipient of the technical assistance support provided through this service contract is the Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the different agencies under its mandate. The ministry of Economy and Finance will receive specific support on public finance management, while the ministries of Water Resources, Employment and Poverty reduction, and Health will also be the object of specific technical support in the topics covered by this contract and under the general objectives of Uzbekistan’s Agri-food Development Strategy 2020-2030.

title-proc.deu: Planting of Seagrass for Ostwind 3 Offshore project between KP18.1-18.4
title-proc.eng: Planting of Seagrass for Ostwind 3 Offshore project between KP18.1-18.4

description-proc.deu: The main target for this operation is the planting of seagrass, either as a single plant or/and as a rope consisting plants. Employer is requesting the Bidder to submit a quotation for the execution of seagrass planting works. The designated location for the seagrass planting is at Ostwind 3 cable route between KP18.1 – 18.4, which is a 325m long and 7m wide (about 2300m²) corridor. Seagrass planting will require the following pre-requisites and follow-ups: A consolidated coarse sediment layer of approx. 20 - 30 cm thickness (engineered material), An execution plan, prepared early enough to achieve the permit in time A permit by authorities (STALU VP, WSA Ostsee), Sufficient plant material seagrass shoots (subject to availability, see details below) to be suitable for planting a harbor nearby (either Thiessow (8km), Freest (11km) or Lubmin (15km)) shall be used for hand-over of seagrass shoots/geotextile ropes with seagrass from Third Party supplier In case it is required the work area per operational day shall be first marked by rods/subsurface buoys attached to small ground weights prior to planting to allow for correct planting spatially and regarding shoot density/m². In case of non-fins-diving solutions it can be done different. shifting of work site day by day shall be enabled by installation of a remote-controlled sub-surface marker buoy with release system on last position of executed work, respectively work executed on previous days shall be inspected by means of underwater video (ROV or UW-drone) repeatedly General assumptions about the task: Total impact area to be restored will be ~2.300m² Work can be executed by divers in accordance with the requirements of DGUV Regel 101-023. Alternatively work can be executed by ROV, if the Contractor can proof the suitability of the technology by references Seagrass planting shall start (latest) on 1st of June 2027 and has to be completed by 31st of July 2027. Employer considers two alternative planting methods: (1) planting of single shoots (2) Installation of rotable fabric ropes with incorporated shoots Suitable ropes ready for installation will be provided by an assigned manufacturer. Single shoot planting planting is the preferred procedure, but rope installation shall be implemented in parallel too. If you are interested in participating in the described procedure, please contact us by e-mail (andre.forbrig@50hertz.com) and express your interest in participating. With the expression of interest, we need the following information from you in order to be able to add you to the project in Ariba: - Full name of the company: - Address of the company: - V.A.T. Number: - Tax Number: - Commercial register number: In addition, I need the contact details of the people who you should have access to the Ariba system: - Name - E-mail address - Phone number

title-proc.eng: RFP 260016 - FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT – LANGUAGE TRAINING FOR STAFF

description-proc.eng: The University of Luxembourg is committed to support its staff members to continuously develop their language competence by providing them group language courses. The courses cover the following languages and levels: - English, French and German from beginner to B2 level - Luxembourgish from beginner to B1 level The language courses are in remote and open to our academic, research and administrative staff across the organisation, and are not intended for students registered at the University. The courses are scheduled to run from March 2027 to March 2031, with two semesters per year. The winter semester typically runs from late September or early October to February, while the summer semester runs from March to June/July. The Contracting Party shall commence the provision of its services in January 2027 and shall, in preparation for the first semester of Mars 2027, make the necessary organisational arrangements in collaboration with the outgoing Service Provider for staff language courses. This preparatory phase shall ensure a smooth and seamless transition for both the participants and the Contracting party. This Call for Tenders is aimed at concluding a Framework Agreement for an initial period of two (2) years and three (3) months, renewable once for an additional period of two (2) years, at the discretion of the University, with a view to retaining, without reopening of competition, a Contracting Party with recognised expertise in adult language training.
